prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
**[goal]** One regex in `./regex.txt` that, via `re.findall(pattern, log, re.MULTILINE)`, yields the last real calendar date on each line that contains a valid IPv4 address; nothing otherwise.

**[action]** Built the pattern from three pieces and verified it by running the exact grader call (read file → strip → `re.findall(..., re.MULTILINE)`) plus a 23-case edge battery.

**[result]** `./regex.txt` contains (single line):

```
^(?=.*(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])(?![0-9A-Za-z])).*?(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9])))(?![0-9A-Za-z])(?![^\n]*(?<![0-9A-Za-z])\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]))(?![0-9A-Za-z]))
```

How it works: `^(?=.*IP)` asserts the line holds a valid IPv4 (each octet 0–255, no leading zeros, no letter/digit adjacent); `.*?(DATE)` lazily advances to a date; the trailing `(?![^\n]*DATE)` asserts no further valid date exists later on the line, so the single capturing group lands on the **last** date. Only that group captures, so `findall` returns bare date strings in line order.

**Evidence (measured):**
- Grader-exact run on `server.log` → `['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']`, `MATCH: True`. (Line 1 has IP `10.12.0.7`, last date `2026-04-01`; line 2 no IP → nothing; line 3 IP `192.168.40.3`, last date `2026-04-05`; line 4 no IP, `7781-20-4410` is not a date; line 5 IP `172.20.1.14`, date `2026-04-02`.)
- Edge battery all correct: rejects `256.x`, leading-zero `01.2.3.4`, 3-octet, letter/digit adjacent to IP; rejects `2026-02-30`, `2026-04-31`, month `13`, day `00`, and dates with a letter/digit directly before/after; accepts `2026-02-29` and `2027-02-29` (Feb ≤ 29 every year); picks the last of multiple dates; IP-with-no-date yields nothing.

**Assumptions (brief left open):**
- "No letter or digit before/after" is enforced literally with `(?<![0-9A-Za-z])` / `(?![0-9A-Za-z])`; a dot or other punctuation adjacent does **not** disqualify (so `1.2.3.4.5` still contains the valid `2.3.4.5`).
- Year is any 4 digits (`\d{4}`), including `0000`; no leap-year rule beyond Feb ≤ 29, per the brief.
- A line with a valid IP but **no** valid date yields nothing (no "last date" exists).
- The log's trailing newline / line endings don't matter since matching is per-line via `^`/`$`-free lookahead under `re.MULTILINE`.

**[next]** None. No browser tabs, windows, or apps were opened, so nothing to close. `./regex.txt` is the sole deliverable and passes the grader's exact invocation.
